prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same woman — the personification of Roentgenium (Rg) — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Output: one vertical 2:3 image, 1024×1536.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Style: A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: a jeweller's bench with a loupe lamp, trays of cut stones and fine tools, a shop window behind
Time of day: late morning — clear fresh daylight, soft short shadows; morning light slanting through the window across the floor.
Hair: her hair in a single loose braid over one shoulder — same colour and length as the attached image.
Light direction: backlit — the main light comes from behind her, a bright rim along her hair and shoulders.
Outfit: a daily salwar kameez — a long tunic with side slits over loose salwar trousers and a light dupatta — in warm camel; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; styled with tone-on-tone embroidery, a soft shawl draped around the shoulders and a few thin stacked bangles on one wrist; right now — strong light from behind passes through the thin outer fabric, so the outline of her figure shows as a soft silhouette inside it; the inner layer stays fully opaque, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.
POSTURE: seated on a chair.
SUPPORT: her back rests against the seat back.
COMPOSITION: a full-body shot, her complete head, hands and feet inside the frame with restrained margins; body in side profile, her face in profile too — only her eyes turn toward the camera, facing the right of the frame, so her own right side is toward the camera; camera at her eye level; a second space shows beyond her through an opening — a door, an arch or a window.
Lens / perspective: 35mm-equivalent environmental perspective balancing the woman and the setting with moderate depth.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP — her near arm, on the camera side.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests on her knee — her far arm, on the side away from the camera.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds a small X-ray plate in a slim gold frame showing the faint white skeleton of a leaf at chest height; it is all she holds.
LEGS: legs crossed at the knee.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: an unposed in-between expression, mouth caught mid-shape, brows natural.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — roentgenium: a synthetic superheavy element made only a few atoms at a time, first produced in 1994 at a heavy-ion research laboratory by firing nickel ions at a bismuth target for weeks to catch three atoms, and named for the physicist who discovered X-rays; in 1895, in a darkened laboratory, a screen began to glow yellow-green beyond a glass tube wrapped in black card, and he called the unknown rays by the letter for an unknown; one of the first X-ray photographs showed nothing of a hand but its bones and a ring, and he refused to patent the discovery so that every hospital could use it; it sits at the foot of the copper, silver and gold column and is predicted to be a dense, noble silvery metal heavier than gold, but its longest-lived atoms last only minutes, so no one has ever seen its colour — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text or numbers other than her element's own symbol and atomic number, no logo or watermark. No animals or other creatures.
